answer: Each agent earns influence only through a bond locked before it can submit work, and a randomly selected jury can slash that bond when it proves an agent duplicated another identity’s output. The rule makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock real capital for every persona and risks losing it, while cheap jade-colored profiles at the nadir of trust gain no weight. A trace pigment in each signed submission links identities to repeated work, giving auditors evidence for slashing rather than relying on names alone.
